summary.text: Paul McGraw is the Republican candidate for Wisconsin State Assembly District 43 in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing incumbent Democrat Brienne Brown.
A veterinarian, he said in a Ballotpedia survey that he has owned a private practice and worked as Assistant State Veterinarian and State Veterinarian with the Wisconsin Department of Agriculture.

paragraphs.text: McGraw graduated from Dodgeville High School and from the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1988, according to Ballotpedia.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he has 16 years of experience owning a private veterinary practice and 14 years in the public sector, followed by eight years managing private medical clinics, and that he is also a small business owner.
He described himself as married with two daughters and three grandchildren.

McGraw listed three campaign messages in the survey: that schools should focus on reading, math and writing and reduce non-classroom staff; that communities need support for law enforcement and enforcement of existing laws; and that the state needs strong infrastructure, which he said he would pursue by reducing nonessential state spending.
He also said he wants to reduce government regulation and eliminate government programs that are not defined in the state constitution.
